title: How do you make a CI pipeline fast without making it flaky?
description: Balancing pipeline speed against reliability: parallelism, caching, test sharding, and how to handle flaky tests without hiding real failures.

data.text: Question: How do you make a CI pipeline fast without making it flaky?

Speed comes from parallelism and caching; reliability comes from determinism and honest test hygiene. Run stages in parallel where there are no dependencies, cache dependencies and build outputs keyed on lockfiles, shard tests across runners, and treat flaky tests as bugs to quarantine — never as a reason to blanket-retry and mask real failures.

items: Fail fast: run the fastest, highest-signal checks (lint, build, unit) first; don't wait on integration tests to tell you a file doesn't compile
Parallelize independent jobs: unit tests, integration tests, and image build can often run as separate runners at once
Cache aggressively: NuGet/npm packages and Docker layers keyed on the lockfile hash; a cold cache should be the rare case
Shard tests: split the suite across N runners by duration-balanced buckets, not alphabetical order, to cut wall-clock time
Deterministic tests: inject clocks and RNG, isolate state per test, order-independent assertions — nondeterminism is the root of most 'flakes'
Quarantine, don't retry-blind: auto-retry once to detect flakiness, then move the test to a quarantine job that blocks release but not every PR while it's fixed

data.code:
# Fail fast + parallel + cached
stages: [validate, test, package]

validate:            # ~30s: catches 80% of breakage before expensive jobs
  script: [dotnet build --no-restore, dotnet format --verify-no-changes]

test-unit:
  needs: validate
  cache:
    key: { files: [**/packages.lock.json] }
    paths: [.nuget/packages]
  parallel: 4        # shard across 4 runners
  script: dotnet test --filter Category=Unit --shard-index $CI_NODE_INDEX

test-integration:
  needs: validate    # runs alongside test-unit, not after
  script: dotnet test --filter Category=Integration

package:
  needs: [test-unit, test-integration]
  script: docker build .   # layers cached on lockfile hash

data.title: The retry trap
data.text: Blindly retrying every failed test makes the pipeline look green while hiding real regressions and letting flaky tests fester. Auto-retry once to *classify* the failure as flaky, then route it to quarantine. A test that flakes more than ~1% should block release until fixed or deleted — a test you can't trust is worse than no test.

items: Serializing everything into one long job 'to keep it simple'
Caching keyed on a fixed name, so stale deps silently persist
Retry-on-everything that turns a broken build green
Sharding alphabetically, so one runner gets all the slow tests
Ignoring a flaky test for months until the team stops trusting CI

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Cache keyed on lockfiles; shard by duration
Determinism (clocks, RNG, isolation) kills flakes at the source
Quarantine flaky tests — don't blanket-retry and mask failures
data.takeaway: A fast pipeline you can't trust is slower than a slow one you can — optimize for green-means-correct first, then for speed.
